back_translation: Behold, you are beautiful, my darling — behold, you are beautiful. Your eyes are like doves behind your veil; your hair is like a flock of goats flowing down from Mount Gilead.
Your teeth are like a flock of newly shorn sheep coming up from the washing; every one has its twin, and not one of them is missing.
Your lips are like a deep scarlet thread, and your mouth is most lovely. Your temple behind your veil is like a split pomegranate.
Your neck is like the tower of David, built in courses of battlements, with a thousand shields hung upon it, all of them shields of mighty men.
Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle, grazing among the lilies.
Until the new day dawns and the shadows flee away, I will go to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of frankincense.
You are beautiful in every part, my darling; there is no blemish in you at all.
Come with me from Lebanon, my bride — come with me from Lebanon. Come down from the peak of Amana, from the peaks of Senir and Hermon, from the lions' dens, from the mountains of the leopards.
You have stolen my heart, my sister, my bride; you have stolen my heart with a single glance, with a single jewel at your neck.
How beautiful is your love, my sister, my bride! Your love is far better than wine, and the scent of your perfumed oils than all spices.
Your lips drip sweetness like the honeycomb, my bride; honey and milk are under your tongue, and the scent of your garments is like the scent of Lebanon.
My sister, my bride, is a garden bolted shut, a stream closed off, a fountain sealed.
Your branches are an orchard of pomegranates with choicest fruits, with henna and nard.
Nard and saffron, fragrant calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of frankincense tree, myrrh and aloes, with all the finest spices.
You are a fountain of gardens, a well of living water, streaming down from Lebanon.
Awake, north wind, and come, south wind! Blow upon my garden so that its fragrances spread abroad. Let my beloved come into his garden and eat its choicest fruits.
